children: Trader Bonk Guy (@theunipcs) responded to criticism over his purchase of EMBER after a Bubblemaps cluster chart circulated widely. According to Foresight News, some users interpreted the chart as showing that more than 50% of EMBER supply was linked to the same address cluster, while others suggested the cluster was connected to him and questioned his motive for buying EMBER.

Bonk Guy said EMBER does not have an internal bundle or internal cluster controlling more than 50% of supply. He explained that the address links shown in the chart came from EMBER's flywheel mechanism, which distributes tokens through an externally owned account (EOA) rather than a contract. Because the EOA transferred tokens to multiple user wallets participating in the mechanism, Bubblemaps grouped the distribution wallet and all receiving addresses into the same linked network.

He said the flywheel mechanism is one of EMBER's main features and distinguishes it from other token issuance platforms. The addresses receiving tokens in the chart belonged to normal users, not insiders. Bubblemaps also suggested that the project replace the EOA with a contract, and Bonk Guy said he hoped EMBER developers would adopt that recommendation. He again denied any connection between himself and the alleged insider cluster.

title: Bonk Guy Denies EMBER Insider Cluster Claims After Bubblemaps Controversy
